summary: Thank you, Sabine. Your answers give us a clear picture, and most of the plan is now locked. Just three quick questions remain, about how a few parts of the site should work.
understood: Priorities: advocacy clients first, then training, then consulting and training for organizations, then care packages.
Families start with a free consultation, simple packages can be bought directly, and organizations get a proposal.
Client accounts include appointments, signing forms online, private messages, case updates, uploading bills and records, paying invoices, and hours used on monthly plans.
CNA course: weekly live online class, online modules with weekly quizzes, a final exam, in-person skills lab and clinical hours, with a deposit to hold a seat.
Store at launch: four care boxes, each also offered without scripture, plus build-your-own. You pack and ship anywhere in the USA.

Your dashboard shows everything daily and handles reminders, forms, scheduling, common questions, student hours and skills, receipts, certificates and payment follow-ups, with reports for your accountant.

followups.question: While your CNA approval is in progress, what should students be able to do on the site?
followups.why: This decides whether the CNA page opens with a sign-up list or with payment.
options: Join an interest list (no payment yet)
Register and pay the deposit right away
Hide the CNA course until it’s approved

followups.question: How should the specialty trainings (dementia and Alzheimer’s, post-stroke, home ventilator, tracheostomy, PEG tube) be taken?
followups.why: This decides whether they live in the online Academy, on the class schedule, or both.
options: Online, at the student’s own pace
A mix of online and in person

followups.question: For the store, how should supplements and shipping work at launch?
followups.why: This decides what the store shows on day one and how checkout adds shipping.
options: Supplements are ready to sell at launch
One flat shipping fee per order
Free shipping over a set amount
